title: doczi: where we are
subtitle: Milestones for doczi itself, tracked with doczi.

milestones.name: First release
milestones.exit: A project can install doczi in Claude Code or Codex, get the rules and skills, and track progress through MCP, CLI and the dashboard on Node.js, PHP or Python.

Workflow skills: plan, implement, delegate, review, ADR, commit
Quality skills: clean code, UI/UX, progress, setup
Reviewer agents: security, tests, UX, performance
Session start: rules and progress line
Edit guard: protected files and AI mentions
Commit, tag and PR text check
Standalone commit-msg git hook
MCP server over stdio
CLI: init, progress, check-ai, git-hooks, projects, serve, mcp
HTTP contract and shared test suite
Node.js, PHP and Python servers
Dashboard with project switcher, paging and themes
Launcher menus for Bash and PowerShell
Plugin manifests and marketplaces for both tools
Pinned upstream plugins: ui-ux-pro-max, engineering
README and API docs
Install into a real project and use it for a week
Verify plugin install end to end in Claude Code
Verify plugin install end to end in Codex

milestones.name: Shared progress for teams
milestones.exit: Two people on two machines cannot both start the same step, and every branch shows the same statuses.

steps.title: Store interface; the file backend moves behind it unchanged

Stale claims are marked and taken over only on purpose
MCP tools and the session start text show holders
HTTP API in all three servers: holder fields, 409 for a held step, claim and release
Dashboard: holder chip, Mine and Held by others filters, stale mark
Branch backend: read and compare-and-swap write with git plumbing, bounded retry
Working-tree file as a git-ignored cache; offline changes queue and report conflicts
CLI: share, sync, claim, release, progress mine
check-status reports plan documents that repeat statuses
Rules and skills: claim before starting; statuses live only in doczi
README, migration guide and the storage plan update

milestones.name: Hosted doczi server
